executiveSummary: Surveillance data spanning November 2025 through May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent communicable disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas Region represents the highest-priority biosafety concern, with ongoing animal and potential human exposure signals reported across multiple PAHO updates. Mpox continues to circulate in the Americas alongside resurgent measles, pertussis, dengue, and chikungunya, collectively straining regional health systems. The start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season in April 2026 adds further respiratory disease burden amid simultaneous RSV circulation.
bottomLine: Multiple overlapping epidemic threats — led by H5N1 avian influenza and mpox — demand sustained surveillance and coordinated regional response across the Americas and Europe through mid-2026.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing H5N1 activity
Animal reservoir detections with zoonotic spillover risk to humans
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential requiring urgent monitoring
Repeated alerts suggest sustained transmission in animal populations across the region
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interface; implement strict biosafety protocols at BSL-3 level; coordinate with agricultural and wildlife agencies; ensure stockpiled countermeasures are accessible

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating ongoing transmission
Sustained circulation across the Americas requiring continued alert status
BSL-3 classified pathogen with potential for human-to-human spread
Continued need for vaccination and case isolation measures
threats.action: Enhance case detection and contact tracing; accelerate mpox vaccination in high-risk populations; coordinate cross-border surveillance; ensure clinical laboratories maintain BSL-3 diagnostic capacity

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 signaling elevated activity
Historical pattern of high case burden in Americas with potential for severe dengue
Multiple serotypes in circulation increasing risk of severe outcomes
Ongoing vector (Aedes aegypti) activity across tropical and subtropical Americas
threats.action: Intensify vector control programs; ensure hospital surge capacity for severe dengue; strengthen serotype surveillance to monitor for hyperendemic transmission

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza (Southern Hemisphere Season Onset)
signals: PAHO alert issued 27 April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Simultaneous RSV and influenza co-circulation alert from January 2026
End-of-2025 Northern Hemisphere season transition reported December 2025
Multi-wave seasonal pattern with healthcare system strain risk
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination for Southern Hemisphere season; enhance respiratory surveillance; prepare healthcare systems for increased respiratory admissions; monitor for novel influenza strains

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 3 February 2026 indicating resurgent measles activity
Risk of outbreaks in under-vaccinated communities following pandemic-era immunization gaps
Americas region had previously achieved elimination status now under threat
Highly contagious with risk of rapid spread in susceptible populations
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination gap assessments; launch supplementary immunization activities in high-risk areas; strengthen case-based surveillance and outbreak response capacity

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated activity
Cyclical resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity
Risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised populations
Increased reporting across multiple countries in the region
threats.action: Review booster vaccination coverage; prioritize Tdap for pregnant women and healthcare workers; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity; investigate potential AMR implications for macrolide treatment

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued 10 February 2026
Arboviral co-circulation with dengue complicating clinical diagnosis
Aedes vector activity facilitating spread in tropical Americas
Risk of geographic expansion into new areas
threats.action: Strengthen arboviral surveillance to differentiate chikungunya from dengue; enhance vector control; issue clinical guidance for differentiation and management of arboviral febrile illness

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
threats.pathogen: Sin Nombre virus / Andes virus (Hantavirus spp.)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025
BSL-3 pathogen with high case fatality rate in pulmonary syndrome form
Rodent reservoir activity linked to environmental and seasonal conditions
Person-to-person transmission documented for Andes virus variant
threats.action: Enhance rodent control and environmental hygiene messaging; train clinicians on early HPS recognition; ensure BSL-3 diagnostic capacity; monitor for Andes virus person-to-person transmission clusters

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3/BSL-4 relevant pathogens have been flagged in this surveillance cycle. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential — was the subject of two separate PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026), indicating sustained animal reservoir activity and ongoing zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas Region; this has been assigned Critical threat level. Monkeypox virus (MPXV), classified as a BSL-3 pathogen, continues to circulate across the Americas as documented in the April 2026 PAHO update, warranting Elevated threat status and sustained biosafety-level-appropriate diagnostic and clinical response. Hantavirus, also BSL-3, was flagged via December 2025 alert with moderate concern. All three require BSL-3 containment protocols for specimen handling and laboratory diagnostics.
amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence may reflect macrolide resistance or treatment gaps in Bordetella pertussis — two PAHO alerts in 5 months warrant AMR investigation
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (PAHO, February 2026) may indirectly complicate antimicrobial stewardship in patients with metabolic comorbidities
No explicit AMR pathogen alerts identified in available report titles; deeper description-level data required for full AMR assessment
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya) in the Americas creates diagnostic challenges and compounded healthcare burden
Dual respiratory virus co-circulation (influenza + RSV) observed both at start and end of 2025-26 seasons, suggesting prolonged overlapping respiratory seasons
Two separate H5N1 PAHO updates within 4 months (November 2025 and March 2026) indicate persistent and possibly expanding zoonotic reservoir activity
Resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) signal immunization coverage gaps likely attributable to COVID-19 pandemic disruptions
ECDC issued five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports (April–May 2026), suggesting sustained or escalating multi-hazard threat environment in Europe
Mpox and H5N1 BSL-3 pathogen co-circulation in the Americas represents an unusually high concurrent select agent burden requiring coordinated biosafety response
